items.readable_text:
Content:
We can easily extend the notion of conditional probability distributions for discrete random variables to continuous random variables.

Content:
For continuous random variables [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y,] the conditional probability density function of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y = y] is given by

Content:
[MATH: f_{X|Y} (x|y) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_Y (y)}, \qquad f_Y(y) \neq 0,]

Content:
and the conditional probability density function of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X = x] is given by

Content:
[MATH: f_{Y|X} (y|x) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_X (x)}, \qquad f_X(x) \neq 0.]

Content:
Notice that these definitions are analogous to those for discrete random variables.

Content:
To compute probabilities, we work directly with these conditional PDFs. For example, to calculate the conditional probability of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y,] we use

Content:
[MATH: P(X \in A|Y = y) =\int_A f_{X|Y} (x|y)\, \textrm dx.]

Content:
In general, the conditional distribution of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y] does not equal the conditional distribution of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X]. That is

Content:
[MATH: f_{X|Y}(x|y) \ne f_{Y|X}(y|x).]

Content:
Finally, if [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] are independent, then

Content:
[MATH: f_{X|Y}(x|y)=f_X(x),\qquad f_{Y|X}(y|x)=f_Y(y).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Recall that the conditional probability density function of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X=x] for two continuous random variables [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] is given by [MATH: f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_X (x)},]

where

  • [MATH: f(x,y)] is the joint probability density function for [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y,] and

  • [MATH: f_X (x)] is the marginal density function for [MATH: X.]

From the equation above, it follows that [MATH: f(x,y) = f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) \cdot f_X (x).]

Now, for [MATH: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1,] we have [MATH: f(x, y)|= f_{Y|X}(y|x) ⋅ f_{X}(x); = (3(x^{2} + y^{2}))/(3x^{2} + 1) ⋅ (3x^{2} + 1)/(2); = (3(x^{2} + y^{2}))/(2).]

For other values of [MATH: x] and [MATH: y,] the function [MATH: f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x)] equals [MATH: 0.] As a result, the product will be equal to [MATH: 0] too.

Therefore, the joint probability density function is the following: [MATH: {3 (x 2 + y 2) 2,|0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1; 0,|otherwise]

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function: [MATH: {x + y,|0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1; 0,|otherwise]

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function [MATH: f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y)] for [MATH: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1.]
sections.readable_text:
Let [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:
[MATH: {x + y,|0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1; 0,|otherwise]

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function [MATH: f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y)] for [MATH: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for [MATH: Y,] we have [MATH: f_{Y}(y)|= ∫_{− ∞}^{∞}f(x, y)dx; = ∫_{0}^{1}(x + y)dx; = [(x^{2})/(2) + xy]_{x = 0}^{x = 1}; = (1)/(2) + y − 0; = (2y + 1)/(2).]

So, the full expression for [MATH: f_Y(y)] is the following: [MATH: {(2y + 1)/(2),|0 ≤ y ≤ 1; 0,|otherwise]

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y=y] for two continuous random variables [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] is given by [MATH: f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y) = \dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_Y (y)},]

where

  • [MATH: f(x,y)] is the joint probability density function for [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y,] and

  • [MATH: f_Y(y)] is the marginal density function for [MATH: Y.]

Now, for [MATH: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1,] we have [MATH: f_{X|Y}(x|y)|= (f(x, y))/(f_{Y}(y)); = (x + y)/(((2y + 1)/(2))); = (2(x + y))/(2y + 1).]

For other values of [MATH: x] and [MATH: y,] the function [MATH: f(x,y)] equals [MATH: 0.] As a result, [MATH: f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y)] will be equal to [MATH: 0] too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following: [MATH: {2 (x + y) 2 y + 1,|0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1; 0,|otherwise]

items.title: Computing a Conditional Probability

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

[MATH: {8x^{2}y,|0 < x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ sqrt(x); 0,|otherwise]

Find [MATH: P \left(Y < \dfrac{1}{2} \,\bigg|\, X=1\right).]
sections.readable_text:
Let [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

[MATH: {8x^{2}y,|0 < x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ sqrt(x); 0,|otherwise]

Find [MATH: P \left(Y < \dfrac{1}{2} \,\bigg|\, X=1\right).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Recall that

[MATH: P(Y \in A \,|\, X = x) = \int_A f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) \, \textrm{d}y,]

where [MATH: f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\,x)] is the conditional probability density function.

Using the formula for the marginal density function for [MATH: X,] we have

[MATH: f_{X}(x)|= ∫_{− ∞}^{∞}f(x, y)dy; = ∫_{0}^{sqrt(x)}8x^{2}ydy; = 8x^{2}∫_{0}^{sqrt(x)}ydy; = 8x^{2}[(1)/(2)y^{2}]_{0}^{sqrt(x)}; = 4x^{2}(sqrt(x))^{2} − 0; = 4x^{3}.]

So, the full expression for [MATH: f_X(x)] is the following:

[MATH: {4x^{3},|0 < x ≤ 1; 0,|otherwise]

Now recall that the conditional probability density function for two continuous random variables [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] is given by

[MATH: f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_X (x)}]

where

  • [MATH: f(x,y)] is the joint probability density function for [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y,] and

  • [MATH: f_X (x)] is the marginal density function for [MATH: X.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We can easily extend the notion of conditional probability distributions for discrete random variables to continuous random variables.

Content:
For continuous random variables [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y,] the conditional probability density function of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y = y] is given by

Content:
[MATH: f_{X|Y} (x|y) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_Y (y)}, \qquad f_Y(y) \neq 0,]

Content:
and the conditional probability density function of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X = x] is given by

Content:
[MATH: f_{Y|X} (y|x) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_X (x)}, \qquad f_X(x) \neq 0.]

Content:
Notice that these definitions are analogous to those for discrete random variables.

Content:
To compute probabilities, we work directly with these conditional PDFs. For example, to calculate the conditional probability of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y,] we use

Content:
[MATH: P(X \in A|Y = y) =\int_A f_{X|Y} (x|y)\, \textrm dx.]

Content:
In general, the conditional distribution of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y] does not equal the conditional distribution of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X]. That is

Content:
[MATH: f_{X|Y}(x|y) \ne f_{Y|X}(y|x).]

Content:
Finally, if [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] are independent, then

Content:
[MATH: f_{X|Y}(x|y)=f_X(x),\qquad f_{Y|X}(y|x)=f_Y(y).]

---

Item 2 — Example: Working With the Definition of a Conditional PDF

Example Prompt:
[MATH: {(3(x^{2} + y^{2}))/(3x^{2} + 1),|0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1; 0,|otherwise]

Consider the continuous random variables [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y,] for which the conditional probability density function [MATH: f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x)] and the marginal density function [MATH: f_X(x)] are shown above. Find the expression of the joint probability density function [MATH: f(x,y)] for [MATH: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Recall that the conditional probability density function of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X=x] for two continuous random variables [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] is given by
[MATH: f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_X (x)},]

where

- [MATH: f(x,y)] is the joint probability density function for [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y,] and
- [MATH: f_X (x)] is the marginal density function for [MATH: X.]

From the equation above, it follows that
[MATH: f(x,y) = f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) \cdot f_X (x).]

Now, for [MATH: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1,] we have
[MATH: f(x, y)|= f_{Y|X}(y|x) ⋅ f_{X}(x); = (3(x^{2} + y^{2}))/(3x^{2} + 1) ⋅ (3x^{2} + 1)/(2); = (3(x^{2} + y^{2}))/(2).]

For other values of [MATH: x] and [MATH: y,] the function [MATH: f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x)] equals [MATH: 0.] As a result, the product will be equal to [MATH: 0] too.

Therefore, the joint probability density function is the following:
[MATH: {3 (x 2 + y 2) 2,|0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1; 0,|otherwise]

Item 5 — Example: Finding a Conditional PDF

Example Prompt:
Let [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:
[MATH: {x + y,|0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1; 0,|otherwise]

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function [MATH: f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y)] for [MATH: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for [MATH: Y,] we have
[MATH: f_{Y}(y)|= ∫_{− ∞}^{∞}f(x, y)dx; = ∫_{0}^{1}(x + y)dx; = [(x^{2})/(2) + xy]_{x = 0}^{x = 1}; = (1)/(2) + y − 0; = (2y + 1)/(2).]

So, the full expression for [MATH: f_Y(y)] is the following:
[MATH: {(2y + 1)/(2),|0 ≤ y ≤ 1; 0,|otherwise]

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y=y] for two continuous random variables [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] is given by
[MATH: f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y) = \dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_Y (y)},]

where

- [MATH: f(x,y)] is the joint probability density function for [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y,] and
- [MATH: f_Y(y)] is the marginal density function for [MATH: Y.]

Now, for [MATH: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1,] we have
[MATH: f_{X|Y}(x|y)|= (f(x, y))/(f_{Y}(y)); = (x + y)/(((2y + 1)/(2))); = (2(x + y))/(2y + 1).]

For other values of [MATH: x] and [MATH: y,] the function [MATH: f(x,y)] equals [MATH: 0.] As a result, [MATH: f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y)] will be equal to [MATH: 0] too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:
[MATH: {2 (x + y) 2 y + 1,|0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1; 0,|otherwise]
